feed.title: Frame & Light

bullets: Roundtables reveal where photographers actually disagree — surfacing real points of contention across underwater, documentary, and commercial lighting work rather than consensus talking points.
Frame and light decisions converge across genres; internalizing that convergence makes the rest of the decisions easier and clarifies which trade-offs are being made.
Practical reliability of gear shows up under crowd-shoot conditions rather than in controlled settings — a pattern observed at teams using Profoto and Peak Design.
Outside of Profoto-class or Peak Design-class tooling, the failure mode is harder to spot, and the second-order effect is the part most people miss.
Ignoring gear reliability and genre-convergence dynamics leads to rebuilding a workflow from scratch a year later — a pattern held across three different teams.
Strobe lighting trade-offs cross-cut every other decision in roundtable photography, making it the point where framing, gear reliability, and genre differences intersect.
Running one idea for two weeks beats adopting everything at once; the rest is iteration.
